title: Wait for Cyclotron retraining rounds on standing runs
description: Dependency on Cyclotron, not Papyrus code: a standing run's accumulated human labels feed a retraining round that produces a candidate context version, evaluates it on held-out votes and promotes it if it is better. Record Cyclotron's API for round status and history here when it exists. Ryan's go for the Cyclotron work happens in the Cyclotron session.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Ryan 11-03 decided how standing runs retrain. Today nothing retrains: hosted runs are frozen and feedback only stores labels. Design: (1) Trigger on evidence of mistakes, not a vote count: per output, score each new vote against the live prediction; retrain when accuracy on new votes is confidently below what the revision claimed, or enough disagreements have built up (confident ones and ones with explanations count most). The requirement adapts: a retrain that gained little raises it, one that gained a lot lowers it. No fixed caps. (2) Promotion is automatic when the new revision evaluates better. (3) While samples are too small to tell, always accept the new revision unless the evidence says it is clearly worse; once there is enough data to tell, it must show improvement. Enough comes from the statistics. This extends the existing provisional-rubric behaviour in staged_optimization.py to the classifier, whose min_development_per_class=20 holds promotion today. Keep the sibling check. (4) Show votes since the last retrain, disagreements, distance to the next retrain and why, and each retrain's before-and-after, in the monitoring page. Owner of the engine change: Cyclotron session.
